runConfig.positivePrompt: Scientific educational image-to-video for ages five to fourteen. One fixed wide camera and one continuous five-second forward-only shot. Preserve the approved first frame and exactly one complete Triceratops horridus with one solid attached frill, two long brow horns, one shorter nasal horn, a closed beak, four planted legs and feet, and one complete tail. Make one clear alert head raise that is easy to see: the animal begins with its head low, then steadily raises the entire skull, all three horns, frill, short muscular neck, throat, shoulder base, and upper chest together by twelve to fifteen degrees. This is one smooth rising arc across the whole clip. The final head and horn tips are visibly higher than at the start and remain at the high pose; there is no return and no second nod. Keep the frill rigidly attached to the skull and distribute the lift through the broad neck root into the shoulders. Preserve horn count, horn length, frill edge, neck thickness, closed beak, eye, skin markings, torso, tail, four feet, ground contact, background, camera, exposure, and crop. The torso does not walk or translate. No reverse, loop, roar, cut, pan, zoom, or background motion.
